MARNELLI T. GA-LAGUMBAY Municipal Local Government Operations Officer Municipality of Impasugong Province of Bukidnon Dear MLGOO Ga-Lagumbay: This has reference to the request for legal opinion from the DILG-Region X on the propriety of the conduct of purok elections. The term "purok" is not officially considered as a local government unit (LGU) under Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC). In local parlance, it usually refers to a geographical zone or division within a barangay. A purok serves as a means to deliver basic services within a barangay, aimed to strengthen participatory govemance and a more efficient public service delivery to grassroots level. A purok may be created or formally recognized by the barangay through a loca ordinance which may specify its metes and bounds, organization structure, internal rules, among others. This is allowed under the LGC which provides that: "Section 387. Chief Officials and Offices. - (a) There shall be in each barangay a punong barangay, seven (7) sangguniang barangay members, the sangguniang kabataan chairman, a barangay secretary, and a barangay treasurer. (b) There shall also be in every barangay a lupong tagapamayapa. The sangguniang barangay may form community brigades and create such other positions or offices as may be deemed necessary to carry out the purposes of the barangay government in accordance with the needs of public service, subject to the budgetary limitations on personal services prescribed under Title Five, Book II of this Code. Section 389. Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, and Functions. - (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance, the purpose of which is the general welfare of the barangay and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the punong barangay shall: xxxx (5) Upon approval by a majority of all the members of the sangguniang barangay, appoint or replace the barangay treasurer, the barangay secretary, and other appointive barangay officials; xxxx "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Section 396. Other Appointive Officials. - The qualifications, duties, and functions of all other barangay officials appointed by the punong barangay shall be govemed by the provisions of Olis Code and other laws or by barangay ordinances." In such instance, the purok shall subject to the LGC which, per the foregoing provisions, can be summarized that: (1) the members of the purok would belong to other appointive officials; (2) their appointments need the approval of the majority of all members of the sangguniang barangay; and (3) their qualifications, duties and functions shall be govemed by a barangay ordinance. Formally established puroks are under the control and supervision of the barangay, particularly the ordinance creating or recognizing the same. We nonetheless acknowledge that individuals may form clusters within themselves for purposes of, among others, efficiency and identification within their own barangay. The 1987 Constitution encourages non-govemmental, community-based, and sectoral organizations that promote the welfare of the nation.l Filipinos are also known to embody the spirit of bayanihan and organize themselves for the common interest of their community. In this regard, the organization may refer to itself, informally, as a purok or other nomenclatures such as a "neighborhood association". Private individuals who create their own group are allowed to set the rules and intemal structure of their organization. Corollary thereto, the Barangay LGU, under the premise of advancing the general welfare of its constituents, may establish, acknowledge or institutionalize their organizational existence through an ordinance. In this regard, the operational structure of the purok relative to the election of its leaders shall be govemed by either of the following: I. Duly enacted ordinance which acknowledges and/or institutionalizes their organizational existence in case of a formally established purok; or 2. The internal rules or procedure/by laws of the respective purok organizations, if any, for informally created purok. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, AUTHORITY OF TH AR B. DINO CRETARY: ersecretary for Barangay Affairs 1987 Constituion, Article II, Secion 23. "hüno, Matunay at MaasahanØ Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54
